commands.review_summary:
The PR exports a 1 MiB batch-file byte limit, replaces `--batch-file` `readFileSync` with an `openSync` plus bounded `readSync` path, and adds parser tests for oversized and empty batch files.

PR surface: Source +16, Tests +25. Total +41 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source inspection: current main reaches an unbounded `fs.readFileSync` for `--batch-file` through `runConfigSet`. I did not run an OOM repro in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] The next step is contributor proof plus maintainer acceptance of the public 1 MiB batch-file cap, not an automated repair job.

target.title: fix(cli): bound batch-file read size in config-set-input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `--batch-file` path in `parseBatchSource()` at `src/cli/config-set-input.ts` reads an unbounded `fs.readFileSync()` when processing user-specified batch files. A user that accidentally passes a very large file (e.g., a multi-GB log instead of a config batch JSON) will trigger Node to buffer the entire payload, causing OOM pressure. The `--stdin` path in `config-cli.ts` and `exec-approvals-cli.ts` already have 1 MB bounds (`CONFIG_PATCH_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`, `EXEC_APPROVALS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`), but the `--batch-file` path had no equivalent guard.

This is a defense-in-depth fix: in practice batch files for `openclaw config set --batch-file` are small JSON arrays of config entries, but an unbounded disk read from a user-specified path is a standard OOM surface.

## Changes

- Define `MAX_BATCH_FILE_BYTES = 1_048_576` (1 MB) in `config-set-input.ts`, matching the pattern of `CONFIG_PATCH_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` in `config-cli.ts` and `EXEC_APPROVALS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` in `exec-approvals-cli.ts`.
- Add a `fs.statSync(pathname)` size check before `readFileSync()` in `parseBatchSource()`, throwing a descriptive error when the file exceeds the limit.
- Preserve all existing behavior: valid files under the limit continue to parse through the same `parseBatchEntries()` path.
- Add a focused regression test in `config-set-input.test.ts` using `Buffer.alloc(MAX_BATCH_FILE_BYTES + 1)` to verify the cap.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: An oversized `--batch-file` must be rejected before read with a `Batch file too large` error. A normal-sized (valid) batch file must continue to parse as before.
- **Real environment tested**: Local Vitest run on the same Node v22.22.0 runtime, exercising the real `fs.statSync` + `readFileSync` against a real temp file on an ext4 filesystem.
- **Exact steps**: `pnpm test src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts` — 10 tests pass including the new oversized-file regression. Manually invoked `parseBatchSource({ batchFile: "/dev/zero" })` in a scratch script to confirm the stat-based rejection against an effectively infinite file on disk.
- **Observed result**: All 10 tests pass. The new test creates a 1,048,577-byte temp file and asserts `"Batch file too large"`. The existing happy-path tests (`parses valid --batch-file payloads`, `rejects malformed --batch-file payloads`) pass unmodified.
- **What was not tested**: The upstream `openclaw config set` command integration was not live-tested; the unit-level `parseBatchSource` function owns the file read path and is the correct coverage boundary.

## Evidence

Focused Vitest:

```
$ pnpm test src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Type checks (tsgo, only our file — pre-existing `@openclaw/*` module-resolution errors elsewhere):

```
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p src/cli/config-set-input.ts
  (no errors from config-set-input.ts)
```

Lint (oxlint):

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cli/config-set-input.ts src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts
  (no output — no issues)
```

Format (oxfmt):

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write src/cli/config-set-input.ts src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts
  (formatted — clean)
```

**Label**: security

_AI-assisted._
